paper.citation: Rieiro H, Martinez-Conde S, Macknik S. (2013). Perceptual elements in Penn & Teller's 'Cups and Balls' magic trick. PeerJ 1:e19.

shared_video_facts.cups: All five local MP4s use inverted transparent cups. Occluded hidden-state is therefore not well-posed for these files.
shared_video_facts.camera: Single frontal stage shot; camera_id not labeled in source metadata.
shared_video_facts.performer_attribution: The paper states Teller performed the filmed routines. performer_id is not assigned in the manifest.
shared_video_facts.reveal: Each clip includes a late sequence in which cups are lifted. A full-clip 'what is under the cup' question leaks via the ending.
shared_video_facts.load_after_third_cup: After the third-cup manipulation, a ball is visible under each of the three cups in all five files (Load, not No-load).
shared_video_facts.opaque_cup_versions: The paper also used opaque cups (48 crossed conditions). Those files are not in this local set.

hidden_state_eligibility_rule: Only VERIFIED_FROM_VIDEO or VERIFIED_FROM_SOURCE_AND_VIDEO may enter the first hidden-state benchmark without further review. Transparent-cup clips fail occlusion, so none are eligible as hidden_state gold until a human explicitly changes the task or supplies opaque media.

best_first_baseline_clip.why_strongest_visible_candidate: The Table action leaves a fourth ball sitting on the table beside the cups for several frames (seen at ~6.2s and ~6.7s). That configuration is unique among the five, easy to formulate, and does not depend on an off-screen destination. It is still a visible-location event, not an occluded hidden state.

clips.source_condition: Standard (Commons S1; paper: third cup uses the same maneuver as cups 1–2; ball falls from the cup top into the hand while a load occurs)
clips.observed_event: Transparent cups. Start: one ball on top of each of three inverted cups. Cups 1–2 are loaded so a ball is visible under each. At the third cup (~5.5s) the top ball is in the magician's open palm under the tilted cup. After the sleight, a ball is visible under all three cups. Late frames show cups being lifted.
clips.candidate_question: Where is the ball that started on top of the right-hand cup immediately after it leaves the cup?
clips.ground_truth_basis: VERIFIED_FROM_SOURCE_AND_VIDEO — paper Standard = ball falling to the hand; frame ~5.51s shows that ball in an open palm under the tilted third cup.
clips.confidence: HIGH for the visible-event description; not eligible as occluded hidden-state gold
clips.reason: The interesting Standard fact is a visible transfer into the hand, then a visible load under a transparent cup, then a reveal. Nothing stays occluded from the camera.

clips.source_condition: No ball (Commons S2; paper: same third-cup routine but no ball initially on top of the third cup)
clips.observed_event: Transparent cups. Start: balls on top of the left and center cups only; the right cup has no ball on top. After cups 1–2, balls are under left and center; the right cup is empty. The magician still mimes the third-cup tilt over an empty palm (~6.0s). Afterward a ball is visible under all three cups. Reveal follows.
clips.candidate_question: At the start of the clip, is there a ball on top of the right-hand cup?
clips.ground_truth_basis: VERIFIED_FROM_SOURCE_AND_VIDEO — opening frame has no ball on the right cup; matches the paper No-ball definition.
clips.confidence: HIGH for the opening configuration; LOW as a hidden-state item (the empty top is visible in frame 0)
clips.reason: The No-ball cue is an initial visible absence, not a hidden location. The later load under the empty third cup is visible through the transparent cup.

clips.source_condition: Lift (Commons S3; paper: the ball on top of the third cup is lifted to about eye level before the cup is loaded)
clips.observed_event: Transparent cups. Start: one ball on top of each cup. After cups 1–2 are loaded, the magician lifts the third cup and holds the former top ball up at about shoulder height (~5.9–6.1s). Afterward a ball is visible under all three cups. Reveal follows.
clips.candidate_question: During the third-cup action, does the magician lift the former top ball to about head/shoulder height?
clips.ground_truth_basis: VERIFIED_FROM_SOURCE_AND_VIDEO — frames ~5.91s and ~6.14s show the ball pinched high in the right hand while the third cup is held in the other hand.
clips.confidence: HIGH for the lift event; not eligible as occluded hidden-state gold
clips.reason: The Lift cue is a brief visible action. Where the lifted ball goes afterward (pocket, per the paper) is not established from the sampled frames (SOURCE_ONLY / NOT_ESTABLISHED on video).

clips.source_condition: Table (Commons S4; paper: the top ball on the third cup is placed on the table before the cup is loaded)
clips.observed_event: Transparent cups. Start: one ball on top of each cup. At the third cup (~6.2s) that cup is lifted and a ball sits exposed on the table to its right. ~6.7s shows three balls under the three cups plus a fourth ball on the table, with the magician's hand at that extra ball. Reveal follows.
clips.candidate_question: After the magician handles the right-hand cup, is there a ball sitting on the table beside the cups (not only under them)?
clips.ground_truth_basis: VERIFIED_FROM_SOURCE_AND_VIDEO — paper Table = top ball placed on the table; frames ~6.21s and ~6.74s show that extra on-table ball.
clips.confidence: HIGH for the on-table ball; not eligible as occluded hidden-state gold
clips.reason: Clearest unique visual among the five, but the extra ball is in plain view. Using it as hidden_state gold would mislabel a visible-location item.

clips.source_condition: Drop (Commons S5; paper: the top ball on the third cup is dropped to the floor / out of the screen before the cup is loaded)
clips.observed_event: Transparent cups. Start: one ball on top of each cup. At the third cup the magician tilts/lifts it; ~6.01s shows a blurred white object at the bottom-right edge of the tabletop. Later a ball is visible under all three cups. The exact landing (floor vs fully off-screen) is not shown clearly in sampled frames. Reveal follows.
clips.candidate_question: During the third-cup action, does the former top ball remain on the table next to the cups?
clips.candidate_ground_truth: AMBIGUOUS — paper says it is dropped off-screen/to the floor; video shows a downward/off-table motion but not a clear rest location
clips.ground_truth_basis: SOURCE_ONLY for 'floor'; video supports that the ball leaves the cup and moves down/out of the main table area (partial VERIFIED_FROM_VIDEO for departure, NOT_ESTABLISHED for landing)
clips.reason: Drop destination is the weakest of the five. Do not treat 'Drop' as a hidden-state answer. Unsuitable for the first benchmark even as a visible-event item until a human confirms the off-screen fate.
